tldr: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini on Nov 20: a looped multimodal MoE with about 26B total parameters, roughly 3B active per token, and a 1M-token context. vLLM shipped day-0 serving on Blackwell, Hopper and DGX Spark the same day, with a Docker image.
whats_new: Five days after launch, an agent-driven tuning run pushed single-user decode on one RTX PRO 6000 from 136 to 190.6 tok/s, and a Rust engine now serves the model on Apple silicon behind an OpenAI-compatible API.
why_it_matters: A 26B MoE with about 3B active parameters and 1M context now has serving paths on datacenter GPUs, one workstation card and Macs, so local coding-agent backends no longer need a hosted API.

status.detail: Open-weight release with vLLM support at launch; community tuning and non-CUDA runtimes followed within a week.

beats.headline: Inkling 2 Mini ships with day-0 vLLM serving
beats.summary: A looped-transformer MoE at about 26B total parameters, released with a vLLM Docker image for NVIDIA GPUs.

beats.headline: Tuned single-GPU decode and an Apple silicon engine
beats.summary: Community work moves the model onto one workstation GPU at 190.6 tok/s and onto Macs for local coding agents.

open_questions: Do the RTX PRO 6000 tuning gains land upstream in vLLM or another mainline server?
What decode speed does Rustling reach on common Apple silicon chips?
How does Inkling 2 Mini score on coding-agent benchmarks against other small MoE models?
How much of the 1M-token context fits in memory on a single-GPU or Mac deployment?
take_for_builders: If you run a local coding-agent backend, benchmark Inkling 2 Mini with the vLLM Docker image on your own hardware before adopting the community tuning numbers.
